newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks rise despite Iraq attack.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks rise despite Iraq attack.

text.p: Jordanian stocks rose on Tuesday as investors shrugged off the impact of the U.S. military strike against Baghdad with a wideheld view that Amman stood to benefit at Turkey's expense, dealers said.

The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.62 percent to 144.80 points from 143.91 points on Monday with the price pickup led by a 4.000 dinar rise in Arab Bank, a major component of the index.
The market shrugged off any negative impact of the U.S. missile attacks against Baghdad, which came after the U.N. announced a delay in the oil for food deal signed in May.
"Investors see this as positive in that hitting Iraq will affect Turkey and could turn to Jordan's advantage economically," one broker said.

Jordan's industrial firms still rely on the Iraqi market to export U.N.-permitted items and the business community says Baghdad has few alternatives to Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba as a conduit for basic foodstuffs.
Many dealers see Turkey, one of Baghdad's major trading partners before the 1990 Gulf crisis, as Jordan's main competitor in clinching future Iraq deals under the oil for food deal.

The market showed few signs of the worries industrialists have expressed over the consequences of the suspension of Iraq's $2 billion oil-for-food deal on Jordan's hopes to gain a substantial share of Baghdad's food imports under the accord.
Along with strong demand on Arab Bank, some buying on select bluechips helped underpin trade after Monday's selling pressure eroded prices.

The market has been underperforming this year with dealers and investors alike pinning the blame on lack of institutional support to cushion the bourse and a high interest rates that have diverted funds to more attractive higher yield deposits.
Dealers said Livestock and Poultry kept up this week's healthy demand with buying interest by a Gulf-based investor reported to have been gradually building up his stake since last week.

A total of 532,916 shares changed hands on Tuesday in a moderate 405,556 dinar turnover in the cash-squeezed market. Of 48 stocks traded, 12 advanced, 17 fell and 19 were unchanged. Four posted year lows.

Investment sentiment has slightly picked up since the government announced last week a package of economic reforms in the wake of recent unrest fuelled by the government's doubling of bread prices in line with IMF-agreed economic reforms.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- fell 0.05 percent to 80.85 points. It was 15.35 percent down on last year.

In industrials, the leading sector, Jordan Cement Factories rose 20 fils to 3.380 dinars, with no signs of the recent limited foreign buying on the stock in which the government plans to sell part of its majority stake.
Livestock and Poultry rose 10 fils to 610 fils on 132,426 dinar turnover. Jordan Petroleum Refinery shed 10 fils to 9.260 dinars.
In services, Jordan Electric Power rose 10 fils to 1.550 dinars and National Portfolio was unchanged at 1.190 dinars.

In banks, Arab Banks four dinar rise to 235.000 dinars was a continuation of recent buying after revived hopes of a bonus share once a new companies law is passed. Islamic Bank was unchanged at 3.580 dinars.

Industrials dominated on Tuesday, with a 330,569 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.02 percent. Banks had a 133,583 dinar turnover and an index rise of 1.16 percent while services had a low 65,815 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.12 percent.
A total of 317,296 shares worth 162,844 dinars changed hands in moderate trade in the parallel market dominated by block sales.
